title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: No new session today (Sunday) — last close was Friday Oct 30's steep selloff: S&P 500 -1.8% to 7,580, Dow -1.1% to 51,770, Nasdaq -2.9% to 25,437, its worst day since June.
Markets: Intel crashed 29% on weak Q4 guidance and tanking PC sales, dragging the AI trade down; Reddit also fell 29% on user-growth worries.
Markets: 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.93% on the tech selloff, capping its steepest monthly drop since Dec 2023; gold slid ~3.7% and Bitcoin fell ~5% to below $77K.

Companies: Binance halted trading after hackers linked to North Korea's TraderTraitor unit stole $6.3B — the largest crypto heist on record; Coinbase shares dropped 12%. No confirmed updates on recovered funds as of this writing.
Companies: Big Oil topped estimates on refining strength — Exxon $15.4B, Chevron $9.9B, BP $8.5B in Q3 profit — while Rivian jumped ~7% premarket on an earnings beat and strong R2 SUV demand.

Companies: DoorDash is pitching its $17B Instacart deal as helping small retailers compete with Amazon and Walmart; Amazon shares stayed pressured after warning of plunging free cash flow tied to AI capex.
Macro/Policy: Three Fed officials signaled support for a December rate hike even after this week's hold at 3.75%-4.00%, keeping markets on edge over the policy path.
Macro/Policy: Labor Dept. finalized a rule forcing PBMs (CVS Caremark, Express Scripts, Optum Rx) to disclose fees and spread pricing starting next July.
Macro/Policy: A bipartisan energy permitting bill is hitting Democratic resistance (Rep. Casten) over fears it favors a natural-gas buildout over renewables amid AI-driven power demand.
